battle.name: 俄國革命
battle.brief: 1905年俄國革命自聖彼得堡工人示威及帝國軍隊鎮壓開始，隨後罷工、抗議與地方起義擴展至俄國各地。此時俄軍主力已轉向栓動步槍；較早的美國陸軍正式型號 Sharps rifle（施拿甫步槍）於1865年列裝，屬後膛單發步槍。

kit.name: 施拿甫步槍
kit.history: 施拿甫步槍是美國陸軍於南北戰爭末期列裝的制式後膛單發步槍，主要供步兵射擊，並曾供遠程射手採用；隨栓動步槍普及，逐漸退居替補地位。

countries: 俄羅斯帝國是1905年這場衝突中唯一從事國家級作戰的國家。交戰的一方是皇帝、總參謀部、陸軍各軍區、禁衛軍與皇家海軍；另一方則是拒絕服從命令的守軍、起義水兵、罷工委員會及武裝戰鬥分隊。芬蘭當時仍是俄羅斯帝國的大公國，並非交戰國，整個衝突也沒有外國正規軍直接進入戰場。戰線最初集中於聖彼得堡、芬蘭鐵路、華沙、里加與波羅的海軍港；冬宮前交火之後，喀琅施塔得、雷維爾、斯維亞博格和利亞帕先後出現罷工或兵變。戰線其後伸入伊熱夫斯克、沃特金斯克等軍械所在城鎮，以及符拉迪沃斯托克等遠東駐防區。六月，戰列艦克尼亞茲波坦姆號在黑海起義；十月，塞瓦斯托波爾水兵控制軍港、巡洋艦與部分沿岸砲位；莫斯科的街區戰則從十月延續至十二月。最後一條戰線沿庫爾蘭鐵路及通往芬蘭的鐵路收束，忠於政府的陸軍與鐵路營恢復交通，孤立尚未被攻下的起義據點。
countriesEn: The Russian Empire was the only state engaged in national-level combat during the conflict of 1905. One side consisted of the emperor, the General Staff, the army’s military districts, the Guards, and the Imperial Navy; the other consisted of garrison units refusing orders, mutinous sailors, strike committees, and armed combat detachments. Finland was then a grand duchy within the Russian Empire rather than a belligerent state, and no foreign regular army directly entered the battlefield. The front was initially concentrated around St. Petersburg, the Finnish railway, Warsaw, Riga, and the Baltic naval ports. After the confrontation outside the Winter Palace, strikes or military revolts followed in Kronstadt, Revel, Sveaborg, and Libau. The fighting later extended into armory towns such as Izhevsk and Votkinsk and into the distant garrisons of Vladivostok. In June, the battleship Kniaz Potemkin mutinied in the Black Sea. In October, sailors in Sevastopol occupied the dockyard, a cruiser, and several shore batteries, while fighting in the streets of Moscow continued from October into December. The final line of operations followed the Courland railway and the railway to Finland, where loyal army and railway units restored communications and isolated uprising strongpoints that had not yet been taken.
people: 皇帝尼古拉二世是1905年軍政體系的最高權力來源，命令經御前會議、總參謀部與各軍區下達；同年九月，他任命尼古拉大公為武裝部隊總司令，但仍保留對軍隊與君主權柄的直接控制。冬宮戒嚴由聖彼得堡衛戍機關、禁衛步兵、禁衛騎兵及哥薩克部隊執行，伊萬·菲利波夫少將等將校在前線協調命令，後來出任內政總督的特列波夫則掌握首都的逮捕與武力部署。地方指揮官的表現並不一致：華沙軍區司令德拉戈米羅夫和駐Finland的布魯西洛夫依靠仍服從指揮系統的團隊恢復鐵路及城鎮秩序；波羅的海艦隊司令艾森與黑海艦隊司令奧西普·菲利波夫則要面對船員抗命。彼得·施密特中尉在戰列艦克尼亞茲波坦姆號上成為水兵的核心人物，後來又在塞瓦斯托波爾組織艦隊和軍港行動。與此同時，伊熱夫斯克與沃特金斯克的士兵委員會、莫斯科罷工委員會，以及各地守軍中的基幹士兵，構成了起義方真正能直接調動的人力。
peopleEn: Emperor Nicholas II was the highest source of military and political authority in 1905, issuing orders through the Imperial Council, the General Staff, and the military districts. In September he appointed Grand Duke Nicholas commander-in-chief of the armed forces while retaining direct control of the monarchy and military appointments. The Winter Palace cordon was manned by the St. Petersburg garrison, Guards infantry, Guards cavalry, and Cossack units. Major General Ivan Filippov and other officers coordinated the forward commands, while General Trepov, who later became Minister of the Interior, controlled arrests and deployments in the capital. Local commanders did not behave uniformly. General Dragomirov in the Warsaw Military District and General Brusilov in Finland relied on units that still obeyed the command structure to restore railway and municipal order. Baltic Fleet commander Admiral Essen and Black Sea Fleet commander Admiral Osip Filippov faced open disobedience among their crews. Lieutenant Pyotr Schmidt became the central figure among the sailors of the battleship Kniaz Potemkin and later organized operations involving the fleet and dockyard at Sevastopol. At the same time, soldiers’ committees at Izhevsk and Votkinsk, the Moscow strike committee, and dependable cadres within rebellious garrisons supplied the personnel whom the uprising could actually direct.
kits: 雙方使用的主要軍械均為俄軍早已列裝的制式裝備。步兵以莫辛－納甘特M1891步槍為主，五發連包一次壓入槍膛；騎兵和後勤人員配納甘特M1895左輪手槍，彈倉容量為七發。支撐射擊使用索科洛夫輪架上的馬克沁重機槍，供應七．六二乘五四公厘俄式步槍彈，並以布製彈帶連續供彈。炮兵包括一四．五公分一八七七年式三線野戰砲與三七公厘霍特基斯一八七九年式速射砲；炮彈分件裝入藥包與炮車，牽引依靠馬匹和炮架前車，轉場則大量使用鐵路。起義者奪取軍械庫後取得的也是同型步槍、彈藥和重機槍，而非另一套武器系統。城市作戰還可見日俄戰爭期間已投入使用的裝甲列車，它保護鐵路、轉運部隊並支援砲兵。海上主力是克尼亞茲波坦姆號，配有十門十二吋主力砲與十六門六吋副砲；奧查科夫號和阿斯科利德號均以六吋艦砲作主要火力。冬季行軍依賴雪橇、馬匹飼料和燃料，春泥季節則受炮車輪距與道路限制；步兵由野戰炊具供應硬餅，重傷者先送團屬救護站，再以馬車或鐵路後送。
kitsEn: Both sides principally used weapons already in Imperial Russian service. Infantry were armed chiefly with the Mosin-Nagant Model 1891 rifle, loaded with five-round packets. Cavalry and support personnel carried the Nagant Model 1895 service revolver, whose cylinder held seven rounds. Supporting fire came from Maxim machine guns on Sokolov wheeled carriages, fed 7.62×54mmR ammunition from cloth belts. Artillery included the Model 1877 three-line 14.5 cm field gun and the Model 1879 37 mm Hotchkiss revolver cannon. Shells were carried as separate components in ammunition boxes and caissons, while horse teams and gun limbers provided mobility and railway carried most transfers. Those who seized arsenals obtained the same standard rifles, ammunition, and machine guns rather than a separate weapons system. Armoured trains already used during the Russo-Japanese War also appeared, protecting railways, moving troops, and supporting artillery. At sea the principal vessel was Kniaz Potemkin, with ten 12-inch main guns and sixteen 6-inch secondary guns; Ochakov and Askold relied on six-inch naval artillery. Winter movement depended on sledges, fodder, and fuel, while muddy spring roads restricted gun wheels and artillery movement. Infantry kitchens supplied hard bread, and wounded men passed first through regimental dressing stations before evacuation by wagon or railway.
tactics: 一九〇五年一月九日舊曆，即一月二十二日新曆，聖彼得堡冬宮前首先爆發正面衝突。禁衛哥薩克騎兵在前列揮刀逼近，近衛步兵封住廣場出口並保持固定刺刀；槍聲響起後，騎兵轉用馬槍和左輪，步兵則依橫線齊射。此後數月，軍方把不穩定的守備營調離首都，並從波蘭、芬蘭和西部軍區調入可靠部隊，以鐵路快速封鎖罷工中心；一旦某團拒絕開槍，指揮官往往先解除其武裝，再由別的團隊接管崗位。伊熱夫斯克與沃特金斯克的起義者控制軍械庫後，利用步兵射線、轉角射擊和重機槍封鎖接近道路，政府軍則以步兵縱隊、騎兵和火炮逐段肅清。六月十四日舊曆、二十七日新曆，克尼亞茲波坦姆號水兵拒絕演習，殺死部分軍官並把艦艇帶離港區；該艦駛往特德拉島時已缺少煤、淡水與食物，岸防砲隊和魚雷艇奉命攔截，雙方隨即發生短暫對射。最後由庫班哥薩克船隻提供補給並護送回港，水兵返抵後遭解除武裝。同期喀琅施塔得、斯維亞博格和雷維爾的水兵也拒絕鎮壓罷工，軍方避免正面強攻堡壘，改以談判換取繳械。十月十日舊曆前後，塞瓦斯托波爾起義水兵控制奧查科夫號、軍港和部分岸砲；十一月十一日舊曆、二十四日新曆，忠於政府的阿斯科利德號向起義艦隊所在水域開火，革命艦隊被迫分散。十月底至十二月初，莫斯科罷工戰鬥隊以路障切斷街口，政府軍先奪取車站、橋樑與電報設施，再把一四．五公分野戰砲展開於較寬街道，以重機槍封住接近線，騎兵控制廣場，步兵逐屋推進；海軍水兵分遣隊也被調入。十二月初六日至初九日舊曆，最後的普列斯尼亞據點被火炮與步兵聯合攻下。庫爾蘭鐵路方面，忠於政府的鐵路營和步兵先恢復車站，再沿線孤立仍在運作的起義武裝。
tacticsEn: The first direct confrontation occurred outside the Winter Palace in St. Petersburg on 9 January 1905 Old Style, or 22 January New Style. Guards Cossack horsemen advanced with drawn sabres, while Guards infantry sealed the exits with fixed bayonets. After the first shots, the cavalry used carbines and revolvers and the infantry fired volleys along their lines. During the following months, commanders transferred unreliable garrison battalions away from the capital and brought dependable formations from Poland, Finland, and the western military districts by railway. When a regiment refused to fire, its commanders commonly disarmed it and replaced it at the post with another unit. After taking the arsenals at Izhevsk and Votkinsk, insurgents used infantry fire along streets, intersecting fields of fire at corners, and machine guns to block approaches, while government troops cleared the area in stages with infantry columns, cavalry, and artillery. On 14 June Old Style, 27 June New Style, the crew of Kniaz Potemkin refused maneuvers, killed some officers, and took the ship out of harbour. Short of coal, fresh water, and food at Tendra Island, the ship was intercepted by coastal artillery and torpedo craft, and a brief exchange of fire followed. A Kuban Cossack vessel eventually supplied provisions and escorted the battleship home, where the crew was disarmed. At Kronstadt, Sveaborg, and Revel, sailors also refused to suppress strikes; rather than assault the forts directly, the government negotiated for their surrender and removal of weapons. Around 10 October Old Style, the Sevastopol insurgents controlled Ochakov, the dockyard, and some shore batteries. On 11 November Old Style, 24 November New Style, the loyal cruiser Askold fired into the waters occupied by the rebel fleet, forcing the revolutionary ships to separate. From late October into early December, Moscow combat units blocked streets with barricades. Government troops first took railway stations, bridges, and telegraph facilities, then deployed the 14.5 cm field guns on broader avenues, covered approaches with machine guns, held squares with cavalry, and advanced infantry from block to block; naval detachments were also brought into the city. Between 6 and 9 December Old Style, artillery and infantry finally took the last strongpoints in Presnya. Along the Courland railway, loyal railway and army units restored stations first and then isolated insurgent bands still operating along the line.
data: 以下日期以俄國舊曆為主，跨越月份之處附新曆：一月九日舊曆、一月二十二日新曆，冬宮前開火；二月十八日舊曆、三月三日新曆，聖彼得堡開始全面罷工，罷工迅速擴展至莫斯科、烏拉爾、波羅的海沿岸與南北鐵路。三月，聖彼得堡守軍中出現抗命；四月三日舊曆、四月十六日新曆，芬蘭車站附近再發生軍方開火。五月，士兵抗命擴及喀琅施塔得、雷維爾與遠東。五月二十五日舊曆、六月七日新曆，伊熱夫斯克－沃特金斯克起義奪取軍械庫。六月十四日舊曆、六月二十七日新曆，克尼亞茲波坦姆號水兵起義；六月初斯維亞博格守軍與七月喀琅施塔得水兵先後拒絕鎮壓。十月十日舊曆前後，塞瓦斯托波爾水兵占領軍港和奧查科夫號。十月十七日舊曆、十月三十日新曆，尼古拉二世頒布《十月宣言》，承諾人身、結社與言論保障及成立國會。十一月十八日新曆，波坦姆號抵達塞瓦斯托波爾；十一月十一日舊曆、二十四日新曆，阿斯科利德號開火後，革命艦隊失去協同作戰能力。十二月初六日至初九日舊曆，莫斯科普列斯尼亞被政府軍奪回，庫爾蘭鐵路戰事亦告平息；十二月至一九〇六年一月，尚未解除武裝的守軍被逐一收繳。一九〇六年春，樞密院程序與首屆國家杜馬運作開始，成為這場軍事衝突之後延續的政治程序。
dataEn: The following dates are primarily given in the Russian Old Style, with New Style added where the month changes. On 9 January Old Style, 22 January New Style, firing began outside the Winter Palace. On 18 February Old Style, 3 March New Style, the general strike began in St. Petersburg and spread quickly to Moscow, the Urals, the Baltic coast, and the northern and southern railways. In March, commands refused by some St. Petersburg garrison units followed the Winter Palace confrontation. On 3 April Old Style, 16 April New Style, troops again fired near the Finland Station. In May, refusal of orders spread to Kronstadt, Revel, and the Far East. On 25 May Old Style, 7 June New Style, the Izhevsk-Votkinsk insurgents seized the arsenals. On 14 June Old Style, 27 June New Style, the crew of Kniaz Potemkin mutinied. The Sveaborg garrison refused to suppress the movement in early June, and Kronstadt sailors did so again in July. Around 10 October Old Style, Sevastopol sailors occupied the dockyard and the cruiser Ochakov. On 17 October Old Style, 30 October New Style, Nicholas II issued the October Manifesto, promising protection of person, freedom of association, freedom of speech, and an elected legislature. On 18 November New Style, Potemkin reached Sevastopol. After Askold opened fire on 11 November Old Style, 24 November New Style, the revolutionary ships lost the ability to coordinate their actions. Between 6 and 9 December Old Style, government troops retook Presnya in Moscow, and fighting along the Courland railway also ended. From December into January 1906, units not yet disarmed were systematically stripped of their weapons. In the spring of 1906, the new State Council procedure and the First State Duma began operating as the political institutions that followed the military conflict.
cause: 衝突的根源不是單一事件，而是日俄戰爭、兵役與財政壓力、勞資衝突及君主權力缺乏代表制度同時累積。俄軍在遠東消耗大量人力與物資，許多 soldiers 被留在前線或剛解除任務，軍中欠餉、裝備不足與官員關係緊張又使他們容易受到政治鼓動。首都與西部工業區的罷工先以工資、工時及解雇爭議為核心，保守派與自由派都反對革命黨使用武裝組織，但政府既未迅速批准全面代表改革，也未解除不准士兵參加罷工等限制，結果使勞資爭議逐漸轉成軍隊是否服從命令的問題。一月冬宮前槍響後，已經存在的罷工網絡迅速聯合起來；罷工委員會要求軍隊中立，士兵則成立自己的委員會，要求改善待遇並拒絕向罷工者開火。地方士兵抗命又為城市武裝分隊提供武器與經驗，使政府每處理一次罷工，都可能增加一批拒絕解除武裝的守軍。由此形成連鎖反應：中央調來更可靠軍隊，地方守軍則因同伴被捕、欠餉與政治宣傳而倒向罷工者，專制政府的鎮壓手段本身成為延長衝突的重要原因。
causeEn: The conflict arose from the convergence of the Russo-Japanese War, military conscription and financial strain, industrial disputes, and the absence of representative institutions. The war in the Far East consumed substantial manpower and material. Many soldiers remained in the theatre or had only recently been discharged, while arrears, inadequate equipment, and strained relations with officers made them receptive to political appeals. Strikes in the capital and western industrial districts centered on wages, hours, and dismissals. Conservatives and liberals both opposed armed revolutionary organizations, yet the government neither promptly approved broad representative reforms nor lifted restrictions such as the prohibition on soldiers joining strikes. Labor disputes consequently became questions of whether the army would obey. After the firing outside the Winter Palace, existing strike networks joined together rapidly. Strike committees demanded that troops remain neutral, while soldiers formed committees of their own, sought better conditions, and refused to fire on strikers. Local refusal of orders then supplied weapons and experience to urban armed detachments. Every strike the government suppressed risked creating more garrisons unwilling to surrender their arms. A chain reaction followed: the center sent more dependable formations, while local troops turned against the arrests, arrears, and political mobilization around them. Repression itself therefore became a major reason the conflict lasted.
impact: 兵變首先改變了軍隊的部署與交戰方式。首都、波羅的海和黑海的多數守軍短期內失去可信度，政府只能把未受革命控制的步兵、炮兵和騎兵集中於大城市與鐵路要點；鐵路營維護車站和通信線，裝甲列車則把可靠部隊迅速送往危機地區，城市內也越來越依賴火砲、重機槍、騎兵和封閉街道中的步兵協同。起義方成立士兵委員會、蘇維埃和武裝防衛分隊，取得軍械庫的步槍、彈藥與重機槍，卻始終缺乏統一指揮、跨區補給和長期防守能力。十月《十月宣言》公布後，部分政治團體接受停戰與合法議會道路，另一些武裝委員會則繼續在莫斯科、塞瓦斯托波爾及鐵路沿線抵抗。政府先以大赦和地方協議換取斯維亞博格、喀琅施塔得、伊熱夫斯克－沃特金斯克及塞瓦斯托波爾起義者的繳械或撤離，之後仍以軍法審判處置已被捕的起義領導者。結果是軍隊內部分裂加深，自由派取得合法選舉與結社的有限空間，而革命政黨也獲得公開組織工人、選舉代表及建立武裝隊伍的制度入口；國會尚未真正建立，軍隊與行政權仍掌握於皇帝。
impactEn: The mutinies first transformed military deployment and methods of combat. The loyalty of most garrisons in the capital, Baltic region, and Black Sea became doubtful, forcing the government to concentrate reliable infantry, artillery, and cavalry in major cities and railway junctions. Railway units protected stations and communications, armoured trains moved dependable troops toward threatened areas, and urban operations relied increasingly on the combined use of artillery, machine guns, cavalry, and infantry operating from closed streets. The insurgent side created soldiers’ committees, soviets, and armed defense detachments. Seizure of arsenals supplied rifles, ammunition, and machine guns, but it never created a unified command, interregional supply system, or capacity for prolonged defense. After the October Manifesto, some political organizations accepted a pause and a parliamentary path, while armed committees continued resistance in Moscow, Sevastopol, and along the railways. The government combined amnesties and local agreements with surrenders or withdrawals at Sveaborg, Kronstadt, Izhevsk-Votkinsk, and Sevastopol, then used military courts against captured leaders. The immediate result was deeper division within the armed forces, limited legal room for elections and association, and institutional openings for revolutionary parties to organize representatives and armed formations. Parliament had not yet gained real control, however, because the emperor still held the army and executive authority.
result: 到一九〇五年底，軍事勝負已相當清楚。普列斯尼亞在十二月被政府軍奪回，塞瓦斯托波爾的革命艦隊在阿斯科利德號開火後失去統一控制，克尼亞茲波坦姆號水兵被解除武裝，庫蘭及其他鐵路沿線的起義據點也逐一被切斷。忠於政府的軍隊最終占據主要城市、車站與交通線，仍控制野戰炮兵、軍港和大部分制式武器；起義方雖曾建立地方委員會和臨時武裝，卻沒有持續控制廣大鐵路與鄉間據點的後勤能力，也無法把各次起義連成統一戰役。外國正規軍沒有參與，使政府得以逐區恢復秩序。政治結果卻不是單純的完全失敗：《十月宣言》承認結社、言論與選舉的合法空間，樞密院程序和首屆國家杜馬在一九〇六年開始運作；皇帝仍保有軍隊、最高行政權及有限選舉制度下的否決優勢。因此，一九〇五年的城市戰役以政府軍取得軍事控制結束，政治危機則以君主讓出部分制度空間、但仍保住軍權與核心行政權告一段落。各次戰鬍的檔案分散且傷亡登錄不全，本實錄不宣稱任何未經核實的精確傷亡總數。
resultEn: By the end of 1905 the military balance was clear. Government troops retook Presnya in December, the Sevastopol revolutionary fleet lost unified control after Askold opened fire, the crew of Kniaz Potemkin was disarmed, and insurgent positions along the Courland and other railways were progressively isolated. Loyal forces ultimately occupied the principal cities, railway stations, and communication routes while retaining the field artillery, naval bases, and most standard weapons. The insurgent side had created local committees and temporary armed formations, but it lacked the logistics to hold extensive railway and provincial positions and could not connect separate risings into one campaign. No foreign regular army intervened, allowing the government to restore order district by district. The political outcome, however, was not a simple total defeat. The October Manifesto recognized lawful space for association, speech, and elections, and the State Council procedure and First State Duma began operating in 1906. The emperor nevertheless retained the army, the highest executive authority, and the veto power inherent in a restricted electoral system. The urban campaigns of 1905 therefore ended with government military control, while the political crisis ended with the monarch conceding part of the institutional framework but preserving command of the armed forces and the core executive power. The surviving records of the individual engagements are fragmentary and their casualty registers incomplete, so this account asserts no unverified precise total for either side’s losses.
